claims: "The Fall Off" is the seventh studio album by J. Cole.
"The Fall Off" is supposedly the final studio album by J. Cole.
"The Fall Off" was released on February 6, 2026.
"The Fall Off" is a 24-track double album.
"The Fall Off" is divided into two parts: Disc 29 and Disc 39.
Disc 29 reflects J. Cole's perspective at age 29.
Disc 39 offers insight into J. Cole's mindset a decade later.
"The Fall Off" was first teased in 2018.
J. Cole described "The Fall Off" as a "full circle" moment for his career.
The "full circle" references J. Cole's 2007 debut mixtape The Come Up.
J. Cole clarified that "The Fall Off" marks the end of his primary narrative arc.
J. Cole's primary narrative arc includes The Come Up, The Warm Up, Friday Night Lights, Born Sinner, and 2014 Forest Hills Drive.
J. Cole retroactively labeled 4 Your Eyez Only, KOD, The Off-Season, and Might Delete Later as "side quests".
J. Cole revealed that "The Fall Off" expanded into a double album following the "algorithm-feeding" events of 2024.
"The Fall Off" debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
"The Fall Off" earned 280,000 album-equivalent units in its first week.
"The Fall Off" marked J. Cole's seventh consecutive No. 1 album.
80,000 of "The Fall Off"'s debut units were from vinyl sales.
The 80,000 vinyl sales set a personal record for J. Cole.
J. Cole clarified that he is not necessarily retiring from music.
J. Cole expressed that he has "nothing else to say as Jermaine via J. Cole".
J. Cole remains open to dropping singles, features, or even another album if inspired.
Future releases by J. Cole would not be part of the official "J. Cole story".
"The Fall Off" features guest appearances from Future, Burna Boy, and Erykah Badu.
"WHO TF IZ U" is the lead single from "The Fall Off" released to radio on February 11, 2026.
"The Fall-Off Is Inevitable" is a track on "The Fall Off" inspired by Nas' "Rewind".
"The Fall-Off Is Inevitable" is told from the perspective of someone looking back at their life from death in reverse.
"Two Six" is a song on "The Fall Off" referencing the area code for Fayetteville, N.C.
Fayetteville, N.C. is J. Cole's hometown.
"What If" is a conceptual track on "The Fall Off" where J. Cole raps from the perspective of Tupac Shakur and The Notorious B.I.G.
"What If" imagines a world where Tupac Shakur and The Notorious B.I.G. reconciled.
J. Cole utilized the Trunk Sale Tour 26 as a grassroots marketing approach.
In the Trunk Sale Tour 26, J. Cole drove across the country in an old Honda Civic to sell CDs directly to fans.
During Trunk Sale stops, J. Cole met with fans to play basketball, listen to the album in their cars, and serve them at restaurants.
A 73-date The Fall-Off World Tour is scheduled to begin on July 10, 2026, in Charlotte, N.C.
The Fall-Off World Tour is scheduled to conclude in Johannesburg, South Africa.
J. Cole released a 2024 diss track "7 Minute Drill"
